boundary: Initialized VECTOR algebra in the exact binary32 subset. These rules do not establish controller numeric rounding, frame transforms, units, kinematics or runtime equivalence.

rules.documented: VECTOR addition/subtraction produces corresponding component sums/differences. VECTOR relations allow equality and inequality only.
rules.implemented: All six input REAL components must be initialized and exact. Componentwise + and - return fresh VECTOR values, and =/<> compare all three component values. No short-circuit equality can hide unknown components. Assignment uses checked copies and stable destination fields.
rules.restriction: No unary VECTOR signs, ordered VECTOR comparisons, VECTOR*VECTOR or VECTOR/VECTOR, constructor or implicit aggregate conversion. Exact initialized aggregate results/value parameters use the routine semantics ledgers. POSITION orientation protections remain in force.
rules.tests: tests/test_vector_operations.py: manual addition, subtraction, equality, copies, aliases, arrays/structures, unknown components and type guards

rules.documented: INTEGER/REAL multiplication and division with VECTOR operate componentwise in both operand orders. Scalar/VECTOR uses component reciprocals; a zero scalar divisor or zero vector divisor component causes an error.
rules.implemented: Scalar converts through the existing exact REAL guard before component arithmetic. Every result uses the shared normal-or-zero binary32 policy. Scalar/VECTOR additionally requires each reciprocal exact and non-underflowing, conservatively covering the manual reciprocal-then-multiply description. Guards precede destination mutation.
rules.restriction: Some mathematically exact quotients are rejected if an intermediate reciprocal needs rounding. Example 7/(7,7,7) is blocked. No assumption about native implementation order, signed zero, error status, axis units or controller overflow/rounding is made.
rules.tests: tests/test_vector_operations.py: both orders and numeric types, narrowing promotion, divide-by-zero, reciprocal/integer promotion exactness, underflow and overflow

rules.documented: Cross # follows the right hand rule and rejects zero or exactly parallel inputs. Dot @ sums corresponding products and returns REAL. Both precede multiplication/division and addition.
rules.implemented: Cross uses the three signed determinants; zero/parallel exact results raise. Dot checks all products and every possible pairwise partial sum before the total, avoiding an unsupported choice of sum association. Product/partial-sum intermediates must be exact binary32 without underflow. Cross outputs also reject underflow. Manual examples (3,4,5)#(6,7,8)=(-3,6,-3) and dot=86 pass. Parser retains highest NOT precedence and requires parentheses for same-level #/@ chains.
rules.restriction: Conservative intermediate guards can reject cancellation whose final result would be representable. Unparenthesized #/@ chains are rejected with E_VECTOR_ASSOCIATIVITY pending same-level associativity evidence. Overflow, inexact intermediates, and compound underflow are rejected without guessing native algorithms or alarms. No magnitude/normalization/trigonometry or POSITION transforms are introduced.
rules.tests: tests/test_vector_operations.py: manual products, operand order, precedence, grouping, zero/parallel inputs, hidden cancellation overflow/rounding and underflow

rules.implemented: VECTOR results are independent writable objects; existing destination references survive assignment. Nested arrays/structures and reference formals retain their contracts. Initialized protected orientation vectors can be read, producing detached results. Bare orientation argument restrictions and recursively read-only destination checks remain. Effectful routine calls inside operator expressions remain rejected.
rules.restriction: No source POSITION orientation initializer is supplied. Read-only operand testing uses a synthetic host fixture only for copy/protection checks. No controller adapter, device read or robot program is executed.
rules.tests: tests/test_vector_operations.py and tests/test_vector_audit.py: destination aliases, protected fixture, function-effect guards, lexical decoys and source/PC drift controls
